newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sandoz wins German okay to buy Azupharma.
newsitem.headline: Sandoz wins German okay to buy Azupharma.

text.p: Sandoz AG said it had received approval from German antitrust authorities to acquire Azupharma GmbH from German pharmaceutical wholesaler Gehe AG.
Sandoz said it had now completed the purchase of Azupharama, Germany's third largest generics company.
"The German regulatory authorities have worked diligently and swiftly. We are delighted that this approval has come so quickly," a Sandoz statement quoted chief executive Daniel Vasella as saying.
Sandoz's purchase of Azupharma for 640 million marks was announced on October 15.

Vasella said at the time the purchase underscored a strategy of making Novartis, the Swiss pharma giant due to emerge from the fusion of Sandoz and Ciba-Geigy AG, the world leader in the fast-growing generic drugs market.
Both Sandoz and Ciba-Geigy already had significant businesses in generics, drugs that are not protected by patents and thus face fierce competition.
Sandoz specialises in bulk manufacturing, especially of antibiotics, while Ciba-Geigy's focus was on retail generics.
Combined with Azupharma, the companies' total generics turnover would amount to some 1.4 billion Swiss francs ($1.11 billion) a year, a company spokesman said.
Based in Gerlingen near Stuttgart, Azupharma employs 440 people and generated sales of 222 million marks in 1995. Branded generics account for 80 percent of sales.
